> 震。亨。震來虩虩，笑言啞啞；震驚百里，不喪匕鬯。

Hexagram 51 is about thunder, and its judgement is about two hands holding two ritual objects while the world shakes.

## 震 is 從雨，辰聲

說文: 震，劈歷振物者 — the thunderclap that shakes things.

Phonetic: 雨 is the semantic side, 辰 the sound.

(Noted: this is the eleventh character in the series taken apart as a picture when it is a sound-compound. The thunder's movement comes from the rain and the noise above, not from the hour-name 辰 speaking.)

## 虩虩: taut, not scattered

虩虩 is glossed as the look of fear — wary, not daring to be loose. (Another account: 虩 is a kind of spider, borrowing the character to describe a person's alarm. Both exist; this book takes "the look of fear.")

And a distinction that decides the whole hexagram: 虩虩 is not being scattered by fright. It is being tightened.

That one difference is the watershed of 震: the shock either tightens you or dissolves you, and the hexagram is about the first.

## 啞啞 is laughter

啞啞 is the sound of laughing and talking.

Which matters: this 啞 is not "mute." Same shape, different word — one is laughter, one is the inability to speak. Read it as "struck dumb," and the sentence inverts.

震來虩虩，後笑言啞啞: first taut with fear, and afterwards laughing.

## 匕 and 鬯

匕 is the ladle used to take meat out of a 鼎 — a ritual vessel, not a dagger. (This is the most commonly misread character in the chapter, and it connects to the previous hexagram: the 匕 takes food from the 鼎.)

鬯 is the fragrant wine of sacrifice, poured on the ground to summon.

So 匕 and 鬯 are the two things in the hands of the one officiating. 不喪匕鬯 — the ladle is not dropped, the wine is not spilled.

震驚百里，不喪匕鬯: a shock that reaches a hundred li, and the two objects in the priest's hands do not move. Which is the whole image of the hexagram: the terror is real and the hands stay level.

## 億 means great

億: great. The 象 supplies the internal evidence, glossing 億無喪 as 大無喪也.

(Another reading takes it as a particle, 噫. This book does not use it, because the 象 has already made it "great.")

## 躋于九陵，勿逐，七日得

六二: the shock comes, and one loses a great quantity of shells; climb the high mound; do not chase; in seven days it is recovered.

The same advice as 復 and 睽: what was lost in a shock is not recovered by pursuit. Seven days is the period, stated.

## 蘇蘇 / 遂泥 / 索索，矍矍

蘇蘇: the spirit unsteady, loosened, coming apart. (Not "reviving" — it is dispersal.)

遂泥: at one shake, falling into the mud. The fourth line, firm in a yielding place, does not tighten — it sinks.

索索，矍矍: shrinking and trembling, eyes darting. Two characters together are a person frightened through: the body shaking, the eyes going everywhere.

## 洊雷

洊: again, doubled. 洊雷 — thunder arriving on top of thunder.

Which states the hexagram's situation: not one shock, but a series. And the response is not a defence, it is the level hands.

## The test

Take the last thing that shook you — a loss, an announcement, a failure. Ask whether you went 虩虩 (taut) or 蘇蘇 (loosened). Then the harder one: what were you holding, and did you drop it.
